rationale: Thirty-first pass: probe the session decision logic that protects the no-more-than-once contract, since a defect there would let a retried proposal reach the state machine twice. The harness registers a client session, asks whether a fresh series requires an update, records a response for that series, then asks again without client acknowledgement and once more after the client acknowledges up to that series. Three CA_EVENT lines record the (responded, update-required) pair and the stored value, which is the exact information that decides whether the state machine is invoked a second time.

investigations.question: Does the session decision logic keep a retried series from reaching the state machine twice, and does it distinguish an unacknowledged retry (stored result, no update) from an acknowledged one (already responded)?
investigations.hypothesis: A fresh series requires an update, a retry before acknowledgement returns the stored result without requiring an update, and a retry after acknowledgement is reported as already responded so the entry is ignored.
investigations.discriminator: The observed (responded, update-required) pairs and the stored value for the three cases.

scope.description: Probe the session manager decisions for a fresh series, an unacknowledged retry and an acknowledged retry.

experiment.prefix: A SessionManager registers client 42 and sets its responded-to value to zero. For series 1 the harness asks UpdateRequired (fresh), records a response with value 9 through AddResponse, asks UpdateRequired again without moving the client acknowledgement, then applies UpdateRespondedTo(s, 1) and asks a third time. Only the session manager is exercised; no raft node, state machine or request object participates.
